title: Min Stack
keyIdea: Store each value together with the minimum of everything up to and including it: (val, min so far). That min never changes while the element sits on the stack, so getMin() just reads the top pair, and after a pop the pair below already knows its own min.

approaches.name: Plain stack, scan for min
approaches.idea: Store values only; getMin() loops over the whole stack.
approaches.why: getMin() looks at every stored value. The problem requires every operation in O(1).

approaches.name: Stack of (val, min so far) pairs
approaches.idea: push(val): new pair (val, min(val, top's min)). pop: remove the top pair. top: top.first. getMin: top.second.
approaches.why: Each call touches only the last pair of the vector. The extra min per element doubles memory but stays O(n).

quiz.q: Why isn't a single "current min" variable enough?
options: After popping the min you'd have no idea what the previous min was

quiz.q: Stack holds (5,5), (3,3), (7,3). What does getMin() return?
options: 3, the second value of the top pair

quiz.q: push(3) when the top pair is (7,3). What's stored?
Why does pop() not need to recompute anything?
options: The pair below was pushed with its own min already saved

steps: Which operations must be O(1)? Are pop, top and getMin ever called on an empty stack?
